title: Wicks, Bodies & Closes
hook: I don't care about the wick. I need the candle to close through the level.

launchpad.outcome: Tell the difference between price reaching a level and price accepting it.
launchpad.missionQuestion: If price wicks above a key high but closes back below it, has bullish structure actually been confirmed?

slides.headline: Reaching a level ≠ accepting it.
slides.line: A wick and a close make two different claims. Today you learn to tell them apart.

slides.headline: A wick reaches. A close accepts.
slides.line: Watch one candle at a key high.

steps.text: The wick pokes above the key high. Price reached the area.
But the candle closed back below. The break was never accepted.

slides.headline: Wick ≠ close.
slides.line: An entire entry model later in the Academy is built on closing past a level, not poking a wick through it.

slides.headline: Two marks. Two different facts.
slides.line: A wick and a close tell you two different things about where price went.

check.prompt: A wick tells you where price ___. A close tells you where price accepted.

options.label: Will go next
options.feedback: A wick is a record of what already happened, not a forecast.

options.label: Was manipulated
options.feedback: A wick alone doesn’t tell you anyone’s intent, just that price reached and didn’t hold there.

options.label: Traveled
options.why: The wick is just the extreme reached, not proof of acceptance.

slides.quote: I don’t care about the wick. I need the candle to close through the level.
slides.line: Say that back to yourself every time you’re tempted to react to a wick.

slides.prompt: Why doesn’t a wick above a level count as a break?
slides.modelAnswer: Because reaching a level and closing past it are two different claims. A wick just shows price visited that area briefly, it doesn’t mean the market accepted trading there. Only a close through the level shows real acceptance, which is why entry rules later in the Academy are built on closes, not wicks.

takeaways: A wick shows reach; a close shows acceptance.
Price can wick past a level and still close back below it, that's not a break.
Close-based confirmation is the rule you'll build entries around later.
remember: I don't care about the wick. I need the close.
